title: Compact maps into generator stages factor through finite thick closure
statement: Let C be a triangulated category with arbitrary coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category], let (E_i)_{i \in I} be a set of compact objects [def-pc-compact-object] (no generation hypothesis is needed), and let X_1 \to X_2 \to \cdots be a sequence such that X_1 is a coproduct of shifts of the E_i and each transition X_n \to X_{n+1} fits into a distinguished triangle Z_n \to X_n \to X_{n+1} \to Z_n[1] with Z_n a coproduct of shifts of the E_i. For every compact object C_0 and every morphism C_0 \to X_n, there is a factorization C_0 \to Q' \to X_n such that Q' belongs to the thick subcategory generated by a finite direct sum of the E_i, where this means the smallest full subcategory containing that finite sum and closed under isomorphisms, shifts, distinguished cones, and direct summands.

source.place: Tag 09SP (Lemma lemma-factor-through), with the notation of Tag 09SN; the generation hypothesis of 09SN is not used in the proof of 09SP and is omitted

proof.text: We argue by induction on $n$ (Tag 09SP). Base case $n=1$: write $X_1=\bigoplus_{\alpha}E_{i_\alpha}[m_\alpha]$. By compactness of $C_0$ [def-pc-compact-object], the map $C_0\to X_1$ lies in the image of $\bigoplus_\alpha\mathrm{Hom}(C_0,E_{i_\alpha}[m_\alpha])$, so it has finitely many nonzero components and factors as $C_0\to F\to X_1$ with $F$ the finite direct sum of the corresponding $E_{i_\alpha}[m_\alpha]$. With $I_0\subset I$ the finite set of indices occurring, $F$ lies in the thick subcategory generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in I_0}E_i$: each $E_i$, $i\in I_0$, is a direct summand of that sum, the class is closed under shifts, and a finite direct sum $A\oplus B$ is a cone of the zero map $A[-1]\to B$.

source.place: Tag 09SP, proof: the case of the initial coproduct X_1

proof.text: Induction step (Tag 09SP): assume the assertion for $X_n$ and let $f:C_0\to X_{n+1}$ be given, with distinguished triangle $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\delta}Z_n[1]$. Since $Z_n[1]$ is a coproduct of shifts of the $E_i$, compactness of $C_0$ [def-pc-compact-object] factors $\delta\circ f$ as $C_0\xrightarrow{g}E'[1]\to Z_n[1]$ with $E'$ a finite direct sum of shifts of $E_i$, $i\in I'$, $I'\subset I$ finite, and $E'[1]\to Z_n[1]$ the shift of the inclusion $a:E'\to Z_n$. Choose (TR1, TR2) a distinguished triangle $E'\to C'\to C_0\xrightarrow{g}E'[1]$; by TR3 applied to the rotated triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] there is $b:C'\to X_n$ making $(a,b,f)$ a morphism of triangles to $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]$. By the induction hypothesis $b$ factors as $C'\to E''\to X_n$ with $E''$ in the thick subcategory generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in I''}E_i$, $I''$ finite. Let $E'\to E''$ be the composite $E'\to C'\to E''$ and choose a distinguished triangle $E'\to E''\to E\to E'[1]$. By TR3 there are morphisms of triangles $(E',C',C_0)\to(E',E'',E)$ (identity on $E'$) and $(E',E'',E)\to(Z_n,X_n,X_{n+1})$ (the map $a$ on $E'$, the given $E''\to X_n$ in the middle), giving $C_0\xrightarrow{u}E\xrightarrow{v}X_{n+1}$ with $\delta\circ v\circ u=a[1]\circ g=\delta\circ f$. Hence $\delta\circ(f-v\circ u)=0$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact](ii) applied to the rotated triangle $X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]\to X_n[1]$ there is $h:C_0\to X_n$ whose composite with $X_n\to X_{n+1}$ is $f-v\circ u$. By the induction hypothesis $h$ factors as $C_0\to E'''\to X_n$ with $E'''$ in the thick subcategory generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in I'''}E_i$, $I'''$ finite. Then $f$ factors as $C_0\to Q'=E\oplus E'''\to X_{n+1}$, the first map being $(u,\,C_0\to E''')$ and the second $v$ plus the composite $E'''\to X_n\to X_{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 09SP, proof: induction across the triangle $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]$

proof.text: Closure (Tag 09SP): put $J=I'\cup I''\cup I'''$. For finite $K\subset J$ the thick subcategory generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in K}E_i$ is contained in the one generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in J}E_i$, since the former generator is a direct summand of the latter. Hence $E'$ (a finite sum of shifts of the $E_i$, $i\in I'$, as in the base case), $E''$ and $E'''$ lie in the thick subcategory generated by $\bigoplus_{i\in J}E_i$; so does $E$, a cone of $E'\to E''$, and so does $Q'=E\oplus E'''$, a cone of the zero map $E[-1]\to E'''$. This completes the induction on $n$.
